title: The Effectiveness of LLMs as Annotators: A Comparative Overview and Empirical Analysis of Direct Representation

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the LLM to generate direct opinion distributions across four subjective text classification datasets (offensiveness, hate speech, abusiveness, and misogyny/sexism) and comparing them against human annotator distributions using F1 scores, Cross-Entropy (CE), and error analysis (evaluating the ratio of False Positives to False Negatives).

Comparing the LLM's zero-shot annotation performance and predicted opinion distributions on the Arabic Misogyny and Sexism (ArMIS) dataset when prompted in English versus Arabic, which revealed a strong bias towards assigning texts to the 'sexist' class when using the Arabic prompt.
